あ: An Apple with a stalk: a cross, then a big loop like the curve of an apple.
1 short horizontal line; 2 long vertical line, curving slightly left at the bottom; 3 a big loop that starts top-middle, crosses the vertical and sweeps round to the right.
お (no cross at the top, the dot sits outside), め (no horizontal line)
い: Two Eels side by side: i-i.
1 the left stroke, longer, with a small hook up at the end; 2 the right stroke, shorter and slightly lower. Leave a clear gap between them.
り (the right stroke is much longer), こ (horizontal strokes)
う: A person bending over with an 'Ugh' — a dot of a head and a hooked body.
1 a short slanted dash at the top; 2 a curve that goes right, then sweeps down and to the left like a hook.
つ (no dot on top), ら (the dot and a vertical start)
え: An Exotic bird with a feather on top and a zigzag tail.
1 a short dash on top; 2 one stroke: across, down-left, then a small zigzag ending in a flowing tail to the right.
ん (no dash on top), る / ろ
お: An Ostrich-like figure: a cross, a loop and a feather (the dot) on the right.
1 horizontal line; 2 vertical line that loops round to the right and back left at the bottom; 3 a small dot top right.
あ (loop crosses differently, no outside dot), す
か: A Karate blade with a little 'ka!' shout mark.
1 a horizontal line that bends down into a hook; 2 a vertical-ish stroke crossing it, slightly slanted left; 3 a short dash to the upper right.
き: A Key: two cross bars and a hooked bottom.
1 and 2 two horizontal bars, the lower one a little longer; 3 a slanted vertical through both; 4 a separate curve at the bottom like the bit of a key. (Some fonts join 3 and 4.)
さ (only one cross bar), ち (bottom curve opens the other way)
く: A beak going 'Coo-coo': one sharp < angle.
One stroke: from the top, down-left to the point, then down-right. Keep the angle sharp.
け: A Keg next to a tap: a vertical line and a little cross with a hooked leg.
1 a vertical line on the left with a tiny hook; 2 a short horizontal on the right; 3 a long vertical crossing it, curving down-left at the end.
こ: Two Koi carp swimming one above the other.
1 a short upper line ending with a small downward flick; 2 a slightly longer lower line curving up at the end.
さ: A Samurai's sword over a little shield.
1 a horizontal line; 2 a slanted stroke crossing it from top left down; 3 a separate curve at the bottom opening to the right. (Handwriting often joins 2 and 3.)
き (two cross bars), ち (bottom curve opens left)
し: A fishing hook — 'Shhh', the fish is biting.
One stroke: straight down, then curve right and up.
す: 1 a long horizontal line; 2 a vertical that makes a small loop below the line, then sweeps down-left.
む (extra dot, loop goes right), お
せ: Say it with a Smile: a cross with a long hooked leg.
1 a long horizontal; 2 a short vertical on the right ending with a hook; 3 a long vertical on the left that curves right at the bottom.
そ: One stroke: a small zigzag at the top, then a long curve down to the left and round. (Often written as two strokes: the dash on top separately.)
た: A Taco: the letters t and a.
1 horizontal; 2 slanted vertical crossing it; 3 and 4 two short lines like こ on the right.
な (a loop at the bottom right), に
ち: A Cheerleader with a curved body.
1 a horizontal line; 2 a vertical that bends and makes a big curve opening to the left at the bottom.
つ: One stroke: across, then curving down and back to the left.
う (has a dot on top), し
て: A Tennis racket handle, or 'te' for the shape of a 7.
One stroke: across, then down in a curve to the left.
と: A Toe with a splinter in it.
1 a short slanted stroke; 2 a curve that starts top left and sweeps down and right.
な: A Nun praying at a cross, with a knot at the bottom.
1 horizontal; 2 slanted vertical; 3 a short dash top right; 4 a vertical that ends in a small loop.
に: A Knee next to two lines — like 'ni' = こ with a stick.
1 a vertical with a small hook; 2 and 3 two short horizontals on the right, like こ.
ぬ: Noodles with a loop at the end (め has no loop).
1 a short slanted stroke; 2 a long curve that crosses it and ends in a little loop at the bottom right.
め (no loop at the end), ね, る
ね: A Nekko (cat) curled up, with its tail looping.
1 a vertical line; 2 a zigzag that goes right, round, and ends in a loop.
れ (ends with a kick, not a loop), わ (ends in a big curve), ぬ
の: One stroke: down a little, then round anticlockwise in a big circle.
は: A Ha-ha laugh: a vertical next to a little loop-cross.
1 vertical on the left; 2 short horizontal; 3 vertical that ends in a loop.
ひ: One stroke: a short flick, a wide U-shaped smile, then a flick up at the right.
ふ: Mount Fuji with clouds: a dot, a curve and two dots.
1 a small dash on top; 2 a curve in the middle; 3 and 4 two dots, left and right.
へ: One stroke: up a little, then a long slope down to the right.
く (pointed sideways). Written the same in katakana (ヘ).
ほ: A Ho-ho Santa: は with an extra top bar.
1 vertical left; 2 and 3 two horizontals; 4 vertical with a loop at the bottom.
ま: A Mama with a loop: two cross bars and a loop.
1 and 2 two horizontals; 3 a vertical that loops at the bottom.
ほ (has a separate left vertical), よ
み: A Me-21: looks like the number 21 with a swirl.
1 a zigzag that ends in a loop, then a long line to the right; 2 a short slanted stroke crossing it on the right.
む: A cow saying 'Moo' with a loop and a dot.
1 horizontal; 2 vertical that loops and sweeps right; 3 a small dot top right.
め: An Eye (me) — like ぬ but with no loop at the end.
1 a short slanted stroke; 2 a long curve that crosses it and ends without a loop.
ぬ (loop at the end), あ, の
も: Fishhook with MOre bait: a hook with two bars.
1 a vertical curve, hooked at the bottom to the right; 2 and 3 two horizontal bars across it.
や: 1 a curve from top left that bends down; 2 a short dash top right; 3 a long slanted vertical through the middle.
ゆ: A Unique fish (yu) with a fin through it.
1 a vertical-ish stroke that loops round to the right; 2 a vertical crossing the loop.
よ: 1 a short horizontal on the right; 2 a vertical that ends in a loop.
ら: A Rabbit's ear: a dash and a curl.
1 a short dash on top; 2 a vertical that curves round to the right and back left at the bottom.
り: A Reed: two strokes, the right one long.
1 a short left stroke with a hook; 2 a long right stroke curving down. (Often joined into one stroke.)
る: A Route with a loop at the end.
One stroke: a zigzag that ends in a small loop at the bottom.
れ: A Ray kicking out its leg.
1 vertical line; 2 a zigzag that ends with a kick to the right.
ろ: A Road with no loop at the end (る has one).
One stroke: a zigzag that ends in an open curve.
わ: A Wasp's wing: a vertical and a big curve.
1 vertical line; 2 a zigzag that ends in a big rounded curve.
を: A wobbly 'Whoa!': a cross and a z.
1 horizontal; 2 a slanted stroke that zigzags; 3 a curve at the bottom right like a backwards c.
お, ち. Used almost only as the object particle, read 'o'.
ん: One stroke: down-left, then up and over in a small hump with a tail.

faq: How do I tell ぬ and め apart?
Both cross a short slanted stroke with a long curve. ぬ ends with a little loop at the bottom right; め does not. Remember: 'noodles' (nu) have a loop, an 'eye' (me) doesn't.
How do I tell ね, れ and わ apart?
All three start with a vertical line. ね ends in a loop (like a cat's curled tail), れ ends with a kick to the right, わ ends in a big rounded curve.
How do I tell る and ろ apart?
Same zigzag; る finishes with a little loop, ろ stays open.
How do I tell さ and ち apart?
Look at the bottom curve: in さ it opens to the right, in ち it opens to the left (like a backwards c).
How do I tell は, ほ and ま apart?
は and ほ have a separate vertical line on the left; ほ has two horizontal bars, は one. ま has no left line — just two bars and a loop.
Why is は sometimes read 'wa'?
When は is the topic particle (わたし は …), it's pronounced wa. In normal words like はな (flower) it's ha. In the same way へ as a direction particle is read e, and を is read o.
What are ゛ and ゜?
The two ticks ゛ (dakuten) voice a sound: か→が, さ→ざ, た→だ, は→ば. The little circle ゜ (handakuten) only goes on the h-row: は→ぱ. Both are written last, at the top right.
What does the small っ do?
A small っ doubles the next consonant — a short pause before it: きって (kitte, stamp), ちょっと (chotto). It's written smaller and lower in the box.
What are small ゃ, ゅ, ょ?
They combine with an i-sound kana to make one syllable: き+ゃ = きゃ (kya), し+ょ = しょ (sho), ち+ゅ = ちゅ (chu). Write them about half size, low in the box.
How are long vowels written in hiragana?
With an extra vowel: おかあさん (okaasan), おにいさん, くうき, おねえさん. A long o is usually written おう (ありがとう), sometimes おお (おおきい, とおい). The dash ー is only used in katakana.
Why does stroke order matter?
Correct order makes characters look balanced, helps you write fast without lifting the pen too often, and makes handwriting readable to others. It also helps you remember the shape.
Which way should strokes go?
Generally top to bottom and left to right. Horizontal lines go left→right, vertical lines top→bottom, and loops in のめぬ go anticlockwise.
How big should a character be?
Fill most of the box — about 80% — with the centre of the character near the centre of the box. Small kana (っゃゅょ) are about half size, in the lower left.
What is the difference between hiragana and katakana?
Both write the same sounds. Hiragana is for Japanese words and grammar endings; katakana (ア, カ, サ …) is mainly for foreign words like コーヒー. Kanji carry the meaning of most words.
Why is を only used in one place?
Modern Japanese uses を only as the object particle (ほん を よむ, read a book), pronounced o. The word for 'tail', for example, is お, not を.
How do I write ん?
One flowing stroke: down to the left, then up and over in a small hump, ending with a little tail to the right. It never starts a word.
Is the っ in a word pronounced?
Not as a sound of its own — it's a tiny stop. Clap it: き・っ・て has three beats, and the middle one is silent.
How should I practise?
Little and often: 10 minutes a day beats an hour once a week. Write each new kana a few times while saying it aloud, then use it in words straight away, and come back to old ones from memory.
Why do some fonts look different from handwriting?
Printed fonts join or separate some strokes: き, さ, そ, り and ふ often look slightly different in type. When you write by hand, follow the stroke order shown in the dojo.
What does 'Word path' do?
It gives you whole words from memory, one kana row at a time. Clear six words without peeking at the guide to unlock the next row.
